headline: Google plans to honor a shared AI training opt-out token in robots.txt
lede: Google says it plans to support a shared robots.txt policy token for AI training preferences, based on IETF AIPREF work. A new Anthropic-authored AIPREF draft describes a robots.txt policy-token mechanism. Separately, Web Bot Auth reportedly reached its first revision since working group adoption.

items.title: Google to support a shared AI training policy token in robots.txt; AIPREF draft describes mechanism
items.body: Google says it plans to support a shared AI training control in robots.txt based on IETF AIPREF work. If a site uses the shared policy token to opt out of training and does not explicitly specify Google-Extended, Google plans to treat that as a Google-Extended disallow. Company-specific controls keep working. Separately, draft-kelley-aipref-training-preference-signal-00, by an Anthropic author, binds preferences to paths with ordinary robots.txt groups keyed by a per-purpose policy token in the User-Agent line. It adds no new directives or grammar.
items.why_it_matters: One robots.txt group may soon express training opt-outs across participating providers. Google has announced plans, not a ship date, so keep existing per-vendor groups and track the token name in the draft.

items.title: Web Bot Auth -01 has origins request signatures with Accept-Signature
items.body: According to agentready.market, the working group's repository logged draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-01 on 2026-10-28. It is the first revision since adoption. As summarized there, every Signature-Agent value becomes a direct JWK Set URI, and the directory, jwks_uri and cimd types are removed. Origins that expect a signature are recommended to request one with Accept-Signature from RFC 9421, and crawlers and user-directed agents use distinct Signature-Agent URLs.
items.why_it_matters: Origins that refuse unsigned requests with 403 should plan to send Accept-Signature. Agent operators using directory-style Signature-Agent values will need to change them.

items.title: OpenWAF verifies dictionary-form Signature-Agent and adds OpenWAF Browsers to its bot catalog
items.body: OpenWAF says its edge now verifies the dictionary form of Signature-Agent from the current Web Bot Auth draft, in addition to the original quoted-string form. A request is attributed only to the member its signature covers. Signed requests from OpenWAF Browsers, previously counted as unverified automation, now appear as the verified bot openwaf-browsers (category AI user agent).
items.why_it_matters: Agent operators sending the dictionary form can expect verification at OpenWAF-protected sites. Site owners can reference the openwaf-browsers id in per-bot overrides.

items.title: Paper finds little evidence that AI search tools fetch /llms.txt
items.body: A paper summarized by ArXivSignals audited 39 sources and found none isolated the security or utility effect of consuming /llms.txt. A purposive 15-tool study it cites observed no automatic requests in 45 trials at one endpoint. A log study found 97% of domains with detected files received no recorded requests in May 2026. Our panel shows llms.txt published by 227 of 276 domains.
items.why_it_matters: Publication is widespread on our panel, but consumption evidence is thin. Check your own logs for fetches before relying on llms.txt as a channel, and treat it as a possible prompt-injection path if you consume it.

items.title: DNS-Based Agent Naming -01 defines AIDISCA and AIINDEX record types
items.body: Verisign authors published draft-seethiraju-dawn-dan-01, Standards Track intended. It describes an inter-domain mechanism for AI agents to locate and connect to each other using secure DNS associations, modeled on DANE (RFC6698). It does this through two new resource record types: AI Discovery Association (AIDISCA) and AI Index (AIINDEX).
items.why_it_matters: This is the first revision after the single -00 version. DNS-based agent discovery implementers should compare it with other DNS approaches before choosing record formats.

items.title: AGTP -10 adds per-request proof of possession and a Delegation-Chain header
items.body: draft-hood-independent-agtp-10 adds per-request proof of possession that binds a verified identity document to a live sender. It specifies a Delegation-Chain header with per-hop scope attenuation and depth and cycle limits, and maps delegation onto the WIMSE chain convention. It also resolves the 262 and 455 status codes and moves module material to companion specifications. AGTP runs on port 4480 with the agtp:// URI scheme.
items.why_it_matters: Anyone prototyping against -09 should review the delegation and proof-of-possession changes and the split into companion specs.

items.title: Google and CopilotKit publish A2UI generative UI integration guide
items.body: A Google Developers Blog post by the A2UI team and CopilotKit's CEO describes building generative UI apps with A2UI and CopilotKit. A2UI has the agent describe an interface as data for the application to render with its own components. The post says CopilotKit provides the chat surface, runtime and A2UI renderer across React and Angular, plus custom renderers for Vue and Slack.
items.why_it_matters: Teams evaluating A2UI now have a documented integration path through CopilotKit for common frontend frameworks.

items.title: MCP Server Cards and Markdown for Agents dip on our panel
items.body: MCP Server Cards are published by 116 of 276 panel domains (-4 since 2026-10-30). docs.ideogram.ai, docs.kombo.dev, docs.n8n.io, docs.tembo.io and docs.adcontextprotocol.org no longer publish them. Markdown for Agents fell to 130 of 276 (-4 since 2026-10-30), and MCP to 133 of 276 (-1 since 2026-10-30). The official MCP Registry saw 1733 servers (3000 versions) published or updated since 2026-10-30.
items.why_it_matters: Day-to-day drops of this size can reflect site changes or fetch failures. Domains that lost discovery files should confirm their well-known paths still resolve.

items.title: Bilateral Attestation draft -03 records cross-organization agent actions on both sides
items.body: draft-mih-agent-bilateral-attestation-03 describes an exchange for agent actions that cross organizations. The requester signs a request attestation, and the performer signs an action attestation recording constraint results and whether the action was performed, declined or escalated to a human. Each side acknowledges the other's attestation. Records can be registered with a Transparency Service for third-party verification.
items.why_it_matters: Teams designing cross-organization agent workflows can review this as one option for dispute-resistant logs, including logging refusals.

items.title: PACT -03 specifies co-signed task contracts and outcome records for agents
items.body: draft-laxsharma-pact-03, Experimental intended, defines signed JSON records for agent tasks. They include a co-signed task contract, a Verdict record bound to the Delivery it judges, and a Facilitator-signed event trace and Outcome Record. A Merkle commitment links a parent's Outcome Record to its subcontracts. Settlement is carried by reference to an external profile, and the draft specifies no escrow or custody.
items.why_it_matters: Agent marketplace builders needing third-party-verifiable task outcomes can evaluate this record format. It leaves payment settlement to other specifications.
